newsitem.title: INDIA: Leader of Indian prime minister's party indicted.
newsitem.headline: Leader of Indian prime minister's party indicted.

text.p: Indian federal police on Monday indicted the head of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party in a $280-million corruption case, authorities said.
They said the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) indicted Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, and 55 others in the fodder scandal in the state capital, Patna.

Last Friday a junior minister in Gujral's two-month-old government who had been accused in the scandal resigned. Chandradeo Prasad Varma, who had quit as junior rural areas and employment minister, was among those indicted on Monday.
The case dates back to the 1980s and involves the alleged siphoning off of funds from an animal welfare programme.
Both Yadav, who is president of Gujral's Janata Dal party, and Varma have said they are innocent.
Yadav has refused to quit as either Bihar chief minister or Janata Dal president, dividing the prime minister's party ahead of organisational elections due by July 3.
